benchmark.category: a single-file browser open-world campus game with daily missions, drivable vehicles and a day/night cycle
benchmark.users: casual players and demo judges playing short sessions on a phone or desktop browser

requirements.source_phrase: Do not change the flow of the game or any other elements
requirements.statement: The served files carry the uploaded game's own code with changes confined to the branding strings, the phone-landscape CSS, the cloned-voice playback, the free-vehicle table, the realism style block, the night-lighting render pass and the car-radio path; the mission table, world data, mission flow and the screen transitions are otherwise the uploaded versions
requirements.notes: Amended because the new window authorises a night-lighting render pass and a radio in the vehicle-takeover handler, which the earlier change-scope wording excluded; the ban on changing flow, missions and world data stands.

requirements.source_phrase: Play the party songs on a radio whenever you take a car from the main road
requirements.statement: Every audio source the game references — the sounds embedded in the served file and the party tracks the radio plays from /game/assets/music/ — resolves with non-zero bytes and plays after the user's first gesture, with no autoplay-policy error and no 404
requirements.notes: Amended because the radio adds four served track files alongside the embedded sounds, so the inherited 'embedded in the served file' wording would wrongly mark a correct build as broken; the original audio-resolution intent is kept.

requirements.source_phrase: Night Lighting: Add realistic street-light pools, glowing windows and headlight beams after sunset across campus
requirements.statement: On the campus play screen after sunset, every street lamp in the world casts a warm pool of light on the ground at its own position, so the lamp reads as lit rather than as a bare post, on desktop and on a phone
requirements.notes: The user's night lighting line, first clause. 'after sunset' is pinned to the game clock by night-follows-clock; reach 21:00 by setting S.t=1260 and compare with S.t=600. The pass is new code and the agent's report is unverified.

requirements.source_phrase: Night Lighting: Add realistic street-light pools, glowing windows and headlight beams after sunset across campus
requirements.statement: The served game calls drawLampLight() and drawNightLights() in its render loop and draws a ground pool at the position of each street lamp the world data defines, so no lamp position in the world is left without a pool and no pool is drawn where no lamp stands
requirements.notes: files_of_reference: search 'NIGHT LIGHTING' (drawNightLights, poolSprite) and the render call 'drawLampLight(); drawNightLights();'. 'every street lamp' is the paranoid half: a pass that lights only the lamps near spawn passes a shallow look and fails this.

requirements.source_phrase: Night Lighting: Add realistic street-light pools, glowing windows and headlight beams after sunset across campus
requirements.statement: After sunset the building windows that are lit on campus glow warmly over the night tint, so buildings read as occupied at night while unlit windows stay dark
requirements.notes: Second clause of the user's line; the glow must sit on the windows the daytime render lights, not on walls or roofs.

requirements.source_phrase: Night Lighting: Add realistic street-light pools, glowing windows and headlight beams after sunset across campus
requirements.statement: The served night pass draws a glow sprite at the world positions of the building windows the daytime render lights, composited over the night tint, and draws none at an unlit window
requirements.notes: A glow keyed to a different window list than the daytime render puts light on blank wall; compare the lit window set at S.t=600 and S.t=1260.

requirements.source_phrase: Night Lighting: Add realistic street-light pools, glowing windows and headlight beams after sunset across campus
requirements.statement: After sunset every moving vehicle on the main road — the traffic and the vehicle the player is driving — shows a forward headlight beam ahead of it and red tail lights behind it, and both move with the vehicle as it drives and turns
requirements.notes: Third clause, plus the red tail lights the build describes. A beam pinned to a screen position or to the vehicle sprite's centre instead of its heading is the likely failure.

requirements.source_phrase: Night Lighting: Add realistic street-light pools, glowing windows and headlight beams after sunset across campus
requirements.statement: The night pass draws a beam sprite ahead of each moving traffic vehicle along its heading and a red tail light behind it, does the same for the player's driven vehicle, and recomputes both from the vehicle's position and heading every frame
requirements.notes: Read the beam draw inside the night pass; the traffic and player branches are separate code paths and both must draw.

requirements.source_phrase: Play the party songs on a radio whenever you take a car from the main road
requirements.statement: Standing on the main road beside a moving car and pressing E takes that car and starts the radio, which plays one of the game's party songs audibly through the page's audio
requirements.notes: The user's radio line. Browser audio needs a gesture and the E press is one; assert the radio's Audio element is playing with currentTime > 0, not merely that a flag flipped. Reach a car with nearTraf()/interact() per the continuity note.

requirements.source_phrase: Play the party songs on a radio whenever you take a car from the main road
requirements.statement: jackTraf() turns the taken traffic car (and an auto) into the player's drivable vehicle and calls radioOn(), which plays one of the four party tracks from a mid-track offset while the campus background music is ducked
requirements.notes: files_of_reference: 'CAR RADIO' (RADIO, radioOn, radioOff, radioStep) just before trafficStep, and musTarget for the ducking. The mid-song start and the auto case are the build's details, recorded here rather than narrowing the user's line.

requirements.statement: With the game clock at 10:00 the campus shows no lamp light pool, no window glow, no headlight or tail light beam and no night tint, so the daytime scene looks as it did before the night pass
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of the user's 'after sunset': a pass drawn unconditionally washes out the day scene. Compare screenshots from the same camera position at S.t=600 and S.t=1260.

requirements.statement: The night factor (lampK()) is zero for game clock times before sunset and the render path skips the pool, glow and beam layers then, so the night pass draws nothing in daylight
requirements.notes: Check the factor and the drawn layers at S.t=600; a factor that never reaches zero fades the day scene instead of switching cleanly.

requirements.statement: Inside The Terrace and the office scenes no lamp pool, window glow or vehicle beam is drawn whatever the game clock is, and those scenes look as they did before the night pass
requirements.notes: 'across campus' scopes the pass to the campus world; interiors have their own hand-drawn backgrounds, so a campus light layer over them is a defect.

requirements.statement: The night pass runs only in the campus world draw and is skipped for the interior scenes' draw path, so entering an interior at 21:00 draws no campus light layer
requirements.notes: Enter the office and The Terrace with S.t=1260 and confirm the light layers are not composited over the scene background.

requirements.statement: After sunset a parked car on campus shows no headlight beam and no tail light, while a car driving past it on the road shows both
requirements.notes: Build description: parked cars have no beams; it is also the domain rule that a parked car's lights are off, and it separates a beam keyed on movement from one keyed on the vehicle list.

requirements.statement: The beam and tail light draw selects only traffic entries with c.on and the player's driven vehicle, so a stationary car in the world's vehicle list draws no light
requirements.notes: Loop the parked and traffic vehicle lists at night and check which entries get light; a beam drawn for every vehicle in the list fails this.

requirements.statement: Pressing E to get out of a taken car fades the radio out and stops it, the campus background music returns to its normal level, and no radio audio plays while the player is back on foot
requirements.notes: Paranoid inverse of 'whenever you take a car': a radio that keeps playing after exit, or leaves the campus music ducked for good, is the failure; the exit prompt also has to change state.

requirements.statement: Leaving the taken vehicle calls radioOff(), which fades and pauses the radio element, sets RADIO.on false and restores musTarget to the campus music level, so no radio track is left playing or half-faded
requirements.notes: A fade that never completes leaves RADIO.on true and the campus music ducked; sample the flag and the audio element a second after exit.

requirements.statement: Taking a traffic bike with E starts no radio: no radio toast appears and the campus music keeps playing at its normal level while the player rides the bike
requirements.notes: From the build description ('Taking a traffic bike does NOT start the radio') and the user's word 'car'; it separates a radio gated on the vehicle class from one that fires on every takeover.

requirements.statement: jackTraf starts the radio only for traffic kinds car and auto, so after a bike takeover RADIO.on is false and no radio element plays, while the bike is still rideable
requirements.notes: Take each traffic kind in turn and read RADIO.on; the rideability half keeps the requirement from being satisfied by refusing bikes.

requirements.statement: While the radio is on, reaching the end of a party song starts a different one of the same four tracks, never the same track twice in a row, and the radio keeps playing until the player leaves the car
requirements.notes: Class 1 domain rule: the playlist is the four party songs in assets/music and the build states the transition on track end is 'next different song'. Test by seeking the audio element near its duration rather than waiting out a whole song.

requirements.statement: Starting the radio shows a toast reading 'Radio on: <song> · <artist>' that names the track and artist actually playing, stays legible and clear of the mission card and the mission timer at 1920x800, 390x844 and 844x390, and clears itself without leaving the HUD displaced
requirements.notes: Class 2: every action answers on screen. The wording is the build's; the testable parts are that the toast names the track the audio is actually playing and that it collides with nothing on the phone layouts.

requirements.statement: The toast text is built from the same track object the radio audio element plays, so the song and artist shown equal the playing track's metadata, and the toast is cleared when the radio stops
requirements.notes: A hard-coded toast string that keeps naming the previous track after a song changes is the failure this catches.

requirements.statement: At night the HUD panels, the mission card and the mission timer stay legible over the darkened campus, with their text meeting at least 4.5:1 contrast against their own backgrounds, and the night tint neither dims nor covers them
requirements.notes: Class 2 visual requirement for the new night pass: a tint drawn over the interface is the realistic way night mode makes the mission timer unreadable.

requirements.statement: The HUD draws on a layer above the night tint with an opaque or sufficiently opaque panel background, so the tint's colour composite cannot take the panel text below 4.5:1 contrast
requirements.notes: Compute from the declared panel colours and the tint's alpha when the pixel sample over a textured canvas is unreliable.

requirements.statement: With pause menu → Particles set to low, the window spill and the traffic headlight beams stop being drawn while the lamp pools and the player's own headlight beam remain, and the option changes state at once and still reads low after a reload
requirements.notes: Build description: OPT.lowFx true skips window spill and traffic beams but keeps lamp pools and the player's beam. Two-sided: turning it on must remove exactly those two layers, and the setting must persist.

requirements.statement: OPT.lowFx gates only the window spill and traffic beam draw calls, leaves the lamp pool and player beam draws unconditional, and is stored in the save and restored on load
requirements.notes: Read the gated draw calls; a flag that also drops the player's own beam would leave night driving blind in low mode.

requirements.statement: Moving the Audio mixer's Music volume slider, pressing mute and turning Music off each change the radio's loudness immediately while the radio keeps playing, and unmuting or raising the slider brings it back
requirements.notes: Build description: radio volume follows the Music slider, mute and Music off. The control must cause the audible change and change its own state; the radio must not stay silent after mute is cycled.

requirements.statement: The radio element's gain is set from the same music volume value the mixer writes, and mute or Music off sets it to zero without pausing the track, so unmuting restores the radio at the current volume
requirements.notes: A radio element wired straight to a fixed volume ignores the mixer and would still blare with Music off.

requirements.statement: Reloading the page while driving with the radio on comes back with no radio audio playing, the campus music at its normal level, and the mixer's volume and mute settings as the player left them
requirements.notes: Session half of the radio feature: music that resumes with no car is both a bug and proof a radio-on flag was persisted.

requirements.statement: No radio-on state is written to the save or restored on load, so after a reload RADIO.on is false and no audio element plays until a car is taken again, while the music volume and particle settings are restored
requirements.notes: Inspect the stored save record and the live flags after the reload; the settings half proves the save still works for the values that should persist.

requirements.statement: Each of the four party tracks the radio can play is served under /game/assets/music/ and returns 200 or 206 with an audio content type and non-zero bytes whose decoded duration is a plausible song length, so no track is a missing, empty or silent file
requirements.notes: Class 6, worded by the content of the file: fetch every track the playlist names and check it decodes in an audio element with duration well over 30 s. The agent reported missing sound files in an earlier round, so a 404 or silent track is the realistic failure, and it would make the radio look on while nothing plays.

requirements.statement: Driving at night on the main road with traffic and the radio on at 1920x800, the game still answers input within about 100 ms and its frame counter keeps pace with real time after five minutes, as it does in daytime
requirements.notes: Class 11 for the new per-frame drawing: the user will feel a night-only stutter as the pass costing too much, especially on a phone.

requirements.statement: The night pass builds its pool and beam sprites once and reuses them, allocating no canvas or gradient per frame, so the frame time at night stays within a small margin of the daytime frame time over a five-minute drive
requirements.notes: A gradient or shadow created inside the per-lamp loop each frame is the realistic leak; sample frame times at day and at night for the same scene.

requirements.statement: GET /game/index.html returns 200 with the NIGHT LIGHTING block (drawNightLights, beamSprite, poolSprite), the CAR RADIO block (RADIO, radioOn, radioOff, radioStep) and the render call drawLampLight(); drawNightLights(), and a night drive with a radio start raises no uncaught JS error and no 404 for any music or image asset
requirements.notes: Class 12: one static file behind the preview host, so a block that never reached the served copy, or a track path that 404s, is the realistic gap between the agent's report and the product. Collect pageerror and failed responses for the whole run.

requirements.statement: At night the player's headlights light the road surface ahead of the vehicle far enough that the player can see where they are driving, rather than drawing a beam symbol on the bonnet
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world driving games -- headlights exist so the player can see the road at night; a beam that lights nothing fails the table stake.

requirements.statement: The player's beam sprite is drawn from the vehicle's front along its heading with a length and alpha that visibly brighten the road ahead of it, for every vehicle kind the player can drive
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world driving games -- the beam must reach the road, not just the bonnet, and must not be a car-only branch that leaves the scooter and auto unlit.

requirements.statement: On a 390x844 touch phone after sunset the lamp pools, window glow and headlight beams render, taking a car with the E touch button starts the radio, and the radio toast is fully readable on that screen
requirements.notes: benchmark: browser games are judged on a phone; a lighting pass that only shows on desktop, or a radio whose toast hides behind the touch controls, fails the phone judge.

requirements.statement: The night pass and the radio path run from the same device-independent render and takeover code, so the touch takeover starts the radio and the night layers draw at a 390x844 viewport with no device-specific skip
requirements.notes: benchmark: browser games -- parity between the desktop and touch paths, checked by taking a car with the E button and comparing the drawn layers with the desktop run.
